In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the DSM approach, as it is presently implemented, is not applicable for the design of cold-formed steel columns experiencing local/distrotional/global buckling interaction, as it is currently implemented in the North-American AISC-LRFD and European EN 1993-1-3 standards.
the DSM expressions for lipped channel columns appear to provide conservative results when applied to columns affected by mode interaction.
the current DSM is not able to provide an accurate estimate of the ultimate strength of columns affected by local-distortional-global mode interaction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the numerical results presented and discussed in this paper are very useful for the development of a new DSM for lipped channel columns.

the numerical and experimental results available to date indicate that, in general, the ultimate strength of fixed-ended lipped channel columns is not affected by local/distortalional/global mode interaction.

, as a consequence of local/distortional/local/global buckling mode coupling, the post-buckled configuration and collapse mechanism of a fixed-ended cold-formed column may be significantly different from the corresponding configuration and mechanism of an otherwise identical column exhibiting a local or distortional mode of buckling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DSM expressions are not able to capture the actual strength of columns affected by mode interaction, as they are not able to reproduce their actual post-buckling response and collapse mechanism.

the DSM expressions are able to predict with good accuracy the ultimate strength of lipped channel columns exhibiting critical-mode initial geometries with a low amplitude, but they tend to underestimate the strength when the amplitude of these initial geometries increases.

the DSM is able to provide accurate estimates of the ultimate strength of the columns considered in the present paper, provided that the column geometries and loading are properly accounted for in the design expressions.
